head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e

findings.claim: The diff removes the four global permission.ask entries 'Edit(**/*.acdsl)', 'Edit(acdsl/**)', 'Write(**/*.acdsl)', 'Write(acdsl/**)' from settings/claude_code/settings.json (deployed to ~/.claude/settings.json, i.e. every repo the user opens in Claude Code). Previously, any Edit/Write tool call touching a *.acdsl file in ANY repo prompted the user for confirmation before executing, regardless of the target repo. The replacement mechanism, cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh (new file, wired into PreToolUse Write|Edit|NotebookEdit in the same settings.json diff), only engages when the repo being edited has an acdsl/policy.json file: it walks up from cwd and does `[ -f "$root/acdsl/policy.json" ] || exit 0` (line 25) — any repo without that file (the vast majority of repos that have not adopted ACDSL) now gets zero prompt and zero denial for *.acdsl edits, where before it unconditionally asked. Even inside a repo that HAS acdsl/policy.json, the hook only denies/blocks rule-file edits (`*.acdsl|acdsl/*`) when mode is exactly 'strict' (lines 47-51); mode 'free' or 'gated' (or a missing/unreadable mode, which defaults to 'free' at line 27) lets rule-file edits through silently with no prompt at all. This repo's own newly-added acdsl/policy.json ships with mode: 'free', so even this repo's own doctrine rule files (e.g. acdsl/rules.acdsl, which encodes the hot-class/security gates reviewed by this very lane) are now editable by an agent in acceptEdits mode with zero human confirmation, whereas before this change every such edit required an explicit yes/no prompt.
findings.evidence: Re-read git diff b4981b88...1f725ced -- settings/claude_code/settings.json: confirmed the 4-line removal from the 'ask' array (previously ask-gating Edit/Write on **/*.acdsl and acdsl/**) and the two new PreToolUse hook registrations (skill-invoke-gate.sh under a bare PreToolUse matcher, acdsl-policy-guard.sh added to the existing Write|Edit|NotebookEdit matcher). Re-read cmd/hooks/acdsl-policy-guard.sh in full (54 lines): line 9 'command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0' (fails open with no jq), lines 21-25 walk cwd upward for acdsl/policy.json and exit 0 (allow, no prompt) if none found anywhere up to '/', line 27 'mode=$(jq -r '.mode // "free"' ...) || exit 0' defaults to free on any read failure, line 28 only continues gating for mode strict|gated, lines 42-45 deny only the fixed self-management-surface filenames (policy.json/policy.schema.json/registry*.json/evalgen.json) regardless of mode, and lines 47-52 deny *.acdsl/acdsl/* only when mode is literally 'strict'. Re-read the new acdsl/policy.json (new file in this diff): 'mode': 'free', confirming this repo itself now permits agent edits to acdsl/rules.acdsl without any prompt, a capability the prior global ask-rule would have intercepted. The claim survives: this is a real, demonstrable reduction in the universal safety-confirmation surface for doctrine/rule-file edits, scoped to every repo that has not opted into acdsl 'strict' mode (which is every repo besides a hypothetical strict-mode one; none of the repos touched by this diff use strict).
findings.fix: Either keep a conservative global ask-rule for *.acdsl/acdsl/** as a floor (removed only when a repo's acdsl/policy.json explicitly sets mode to something other than free), or change acdsl-policy-guard.sh's default-missing-file and default-missing-mode behavior to deny-by-default (fail closed) for the self-management surface and rule files rather than silently falling through to free/allow.

notes: Cross-chunk suspicion for the station: the settings.json/acdsl-policy-guard.sh finding (security-MAJ-1) also touches cmd/acdsl/main.go and internal/acdsl/policy.go (bin/acdsl CheckPolicy, the authoritative enforcement acdsl-policy-guard.sh's own comment defers to), which are outside this chunk — this lane could not verify whether bin/acdsl's own CheckPolicy independently blocks *.acdsl writes in free/gated mode at commit time or audit time as a compensating control; flagging for the station/other chunk's lane to confirm or refute.
